title: Charter of Ban Kulin
place: Bosnia (place of writing unknown; shown at Visoko)
description: Ban Kulin grants merchants of Dubrovnik free trade in his land, in the oldest surviving document of the Bosnian state.

title: Abjuration at Bilino Polje
description: Ban Kulin and the leaders of the Bosnian Church renounce heresy before a papal legate, heading off a crusade against Bosnia.

title: Tvrtko I crowned king
description: Ban Tvrtko I is crowned king, raising Bosnia to a kingdom that becomes the strongest state in the western Balkans.

title: Sarajevo founded
description: The Ottoman governor Isa-Beg Ishaković endows a mosque, market and bridge that grow into the city of Sarajevo.

title: Ottoman conquest of Bosnia
description: Mehmed II overruns the kingdom and has the last king, Stephen Tomašević, beheaded, beginning four centuries of Ottoman rule.

title: Ahdname of Milodraž
description: Mehmed II grants the Bosnian Franciscans freedom to practise their faith, a charter still kept at Fojnica.

title: Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque built
description: The governor Gazi Husrev-beg completes the main mosque of Sarajevo, the centre of an endowment that shapes the city.

title: Old Bridge of Mostar completed
description: Mimar Hayruddin finishes a single stone arch over the Neretva that gives the town of Mostar its name and symbol.

title: Bridge on the Drina completed
description: The court architect Sinan completes an eleven-arch bridge at Višegrad for the grand vizier Mehmed Pasha Sokolović.

title: Sack of Sarajevo
description: A Habsburg raiding force under Prince Eugene of Savoy plunders and burns Sarajevo, leaving most of the city in ruins.

title: Battle of Banja Luka
description: Bosnian troops under Hekimoğlu Ali Pasha defeat an invading Austrian army, keeping Bosnia in the Ottoman Empire.

title: Bosnian uprising
description: Bosnian notables led by Husein Gradaščević rise against the sultan's reforms and demand autonomy before being defeated near Sarajevo.

title: Herzegovina uprising
description: A clash at Nevesinje begins a revolt of Christian peasants against Ottoman taxes that spreads through the region and opens the crisis that ends Ottoman rule in Bosnia.

title: Austro-Hungarian troops take Sarajevo
description: Austria-Hungary, given the right to occupy Bosnia and Herzegovina by the Congress of Berlin, captures Sarajevo against armed local resistance.

title: Annexation by Austria-Hungary
description: Austria-Hungary announces the annexation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, setting off a European crisis and embittering Serbia.

title: Battle of the Sutjeska
description: Axis forces begin an offensive to encircle Tito's Partisans, who break out a month later with heavy losses.

title: First session of ZAVNOBiH
description: A Partisan assembly declares Bosnia and Herzegovina a common land of Serbs, Muslims and Croats, a date now kept as Statehood Day.

title: Second session of AVNOJ
description: The Partisan council meeting at Jajce resolves to rebuild Yugoslavia as a federation of six republics, one of them Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: Sarajevo Winter Olympics
description: The Winter Olympic Games open in Sarajevo, the first Winter Games held in a socialist country.

title: Independence referendum
description: Voters back independence from Yugoslavia in a referendum boycotted by most Bosnian Serbs, and war follows within weeks.

title: Siege of Sarajevo
description: Bosnian Serb forces surround and shell the capital for almost four years, the longest siege of a capital city in modern warfare.

title: Old Bridge of Mostar destroyed
description: Bosnian Croat artillery brings down the sixteenth-century bridge during fighting between Croats and Bosniaks.

title: Washington Agreement
description: Bosniak and Bosnian Croat leaders end their war and form the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: Srebrenica massacre
description: Bosnian Serb forces take the United Nations safe area of Srebrenica and kill more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys, later ruled a genocide.

title: Dayton Agreement
description: The presidents of Bosnia, Serbia and Croatia agree a peace that ends the war and divides the country into two entities.

title: Rebuilt Old Bridge opens
description: The reconstructed Old Bridge is opened, and it is listed as a World Heritage Site the following year.

title: Unrest of 2014
description: Protests by laid-off factory workers in Tuzla spread to other cities, where government buildings are set on fire.
